perf.summary: Same n/i bound substitution to remove the per-iteration 64-bit multiply.
perf.currentCost: prod = (long)i * primes[j] each inner iteration; used only for the bound test and as the index maxPrime[(int)prod].
perf.proposedChange: int lim = n / i; once per i; inner: if (primes[j] > lim) break; maxPrime[i * primes[j]] = maxPrime[i]; if (i % primes[j] == 0) break;
perf.rationale: One division per outer i replaces a 64-bit multiply + 64-bit compare per inner iteration; the kept multiply is 32-bit and provably non-overflowing (<= n). This is the simplest of the three sieves so the relative win is largest.
perf.risk: None; primes[j] <= n/i is the exact equivalent break for positive ints, and i*primes[j] <= n fits int. maxPrime[i] is loop-invariant within the inner loop and can additionally be hoisted into a local (int mpi = maxPrime[i];).

perf.summary: Hoist maxPrime[i] into a local across the inner loop.
perf.currentCost: maxPrime[(int)prod] = maxPrime[i]; reloads maxPrime[i] every inner iteration; the store target index (i*primes[j] >= 2i) never equals i, but the compiler may not prove non-aliasing through int*.
perf.proposedChange: int mpi = maxPrime[i]; before the inner loop; then maxPrime[i*primes[j]] = mpi;
perf.rationale: Guarantees a single load of maxPrime[i] instead of one per inner iteration, removing a load-after-store hazard the optimizer cannot always discharge.
perf.risk: None; write index >= 2i > i so maxPrime[i] is never overwritten inside the inner loop. Same output.
